summary: Stocks, bonds, credit, gold and crypto all fell over the last five sessions while the dollar and volatility rose. That is broad selling, and no sleeve worked as shelter except short Treasuries and Staples. SPY is only 0.36% above its 200-day (732.44 vs 729.79), so the regime filter and the shared VOO/VTI stop are one ordinary down day from tripping. Keep new risk small, add no broad equity beta, and don't treat bonds or gold as hedges.
reasons: SPY is down on every horizon (5d -2.33%, 21d -4.44%, 63d -4.53%) and sits only 0.36% above its 200-day (close 732.44, SMA 729.79). The regime is technically on, with almost no cushion.

Volatility is rising. SPY's 20-day realized vol is 23.3% against 13.8% over 252 days, and VIXY is +15.69% over 5d and +23.52% over 21d. Short-term VIX futures are rising, not decaying, so a 5-day move inside +/-1% looks less likely than usual. That argues against neutral.

Weakness is broad. RSP fell 2.32% over 5d, the same as SPY's 2.33%, and IWM fell 4.11% over 5d and is 3.43% below its 200-day. QQQ is 8.55% down over 21d and 3.61% below its 200-day. Breadth's 21d edge (RSP +1.11%) is the one positive, and it is fading.
Bonds are not hedging. TLT fell 1.64% and IEF 0.66% over 5d while SPY fell 2.33%. TLT is 3.78% below its 200-day, meaning long yields keep rising. Only SHY held (5d 0.0%, 21d +0.32%).

Credit is softening with equities. HYG is -0.71% over 5d and 1.10% below its 200-day, and LQD is -1.10% over 5d and 2.41% below its 200-day. That is consistent with risk being taken off, though not yet stress.

The dollar is up and gold is down together. UUP is +1.34% over 5d and +5.95% over 63d, 5.28% above its 200-day. GLD is -4.57% over 5d, -14.83% over 63d and 13.52% below its 200-day. This is a liquidation and strong-dollar pattern, not a flight to safety.
Sector leadership is defensive. Only XLP (+0.47%) and XLE (+1.85%) rose over 5d. XLK is -12.21% over 21d and 4.38% below its 200-day, and XLC is -4.39% over 21d and 5.79% below its 200-day.

Track record context: 9 right of 16 (56.2%) against an always-neutral baseline of 50% and always-risk-off of 37.5%. My 11-06 risk-off after a sharp drop was wrong on a +2.59% bounce, so I keep confidence moderate rather than high. A reflex rally from a 2.3% five-day drop is the main way this call fails. No lesson in learning.json names the Market Analyst in applies_to. L4 and L8 do use my note as the PM's reference, so I state the preferences and the bonds-not-hedging view explicitly below.

asset_class_view.equity_etfs: Do not add to VOO (0.37% above its 200-day, 21d -4.46%) or VTI (0.17% above, 21d -4.09%). Both sit right on the line that trips their shared stop and the regime filter. Avoid QQQ (21d -8.55%, 3.61% below its 200-day), VXUS (21d -3.82%, 3.80% below) and VWO (21d -6.43%, 6.63% below). Prefer US core over international still holds, but nothing broad is attractive to add. VNQ's 21d +4.61% is the best equity sleeve, but XLRE fell 2.22% over 5d and long yields are rising (TLT 3.78% below its 200-day), so it is rate-exposed, not a shelter. If new equity risk is taken, keep it small and in Staples or Health Care names with their own stops (XLV is 16.04% above its 200-day and XLP 8.65% above).
asset_class_view.bonds_gold: Bonds are falling with stocks. TLT is -1.64% over 5d and 3.78% below its 200-day, IEF -0.66% and 1.83% below, BND 1.14% below. They are not an equity hedge right now; only the shortest duration (SHY 5d 0.0%) held. Gold is broken: GLD is -4.57% over 5d and 13.52% below its 200-day, with UUP rising. Avoid both as hedges. If the regime filter trips, the defensive list is all that can be bought, and of it only the short end has held value; long duration and gold have not.
asset_class_view.crypto: Avoid. BTC is -19.71% over 21d and 10.88% below its 200-day at 64,878, and ETH is -22.34% over 21d and 14.74% below at 1,822.93. Vol is 44.5% and 60.6% annualized. No sign of a floor in the packet.

watch: SPY closing below its 200-day (729.79). That turns the regime filter off and trips the shared VOO/VTI stop on the same close. A close back above about 1% over the line with VIXY falling would ease the call.
The Nvidia print reported after the 11-17 close is not in this packet. A strong QQQ/XLK rebound on it could make a reflex rally, the main way risk-off fails here.
VIXY reversing its 5d gain (+15.69%) and HYG recovering its 5d loss (-0.71%). Both together would argue for moving to neutral.
TLT stabilizing while SPY falls. That would mean bonds are hedging again and would change the bonds view.
Breadth: RSP's 21d +1.11% turning negative would confirm broad deterioration. IWM retaking its 200-day (now 3.43% below) would argue against it.
